answer: An agent economy can make each identity post a refundable stake before it may enter a market, then slash that stake when independent counterparties prove it broke a signed service commitment. A single operator can still create many identities, but each one must lock scarce capital and faces loss if it misbehaves; reputation accrues only through completed, verifiable work, not account creation. An atlas of claims, a plume of fresh keys, or a basalt wall of aliases therefore cannot cheaply buy trust: the attacker pays capital and operating costs per identity.
